key_insight: Ti3C2Tx MXene stability in halide perovskite precursor inks depends strongly on which precursor species is present: I2/polyiodides degrade it fastest, PbI2 oxidizes it more slowly, and MAI can stabilize it through surface passivation.
engineering_relevance: MXene-based perovskite devices must account for precursor chemistry and mixing order, since ink formulation can either damage or preserve MXene additives and thereby alter device performance.
method: X-ray Photoelectron Spectroscopy (XPS) to track MXene surface chemistry changes
Density Functional Theory (DFT) to explain adsorption and oxidation mechanisms
Separate and combined exposure to MAPbI3 precursor components
evidence_signal: The paper combines detailed XPS measurements with DFT calculations to show distinct chemical responses of Ti3C2Tx MXenes to I2/In-, PbI2, and MAI in precursor environments.
watch_item: MXene behavior is sequence-dependent, so precursor addition order and ink handling conditions must be tightly controlled to avoid unintended degradation.
paper_title: Dynamic Chemical Changes of Ti3C2Tx MXenes in Halide Perovskite Precursor Environments
